projects.desc: Shared memory for AI agents: bi-temporal facts, first-class decision units, and conflicts that stay pending until the owner rules.
projects.long: Mirsad gives AI agents a shared, living memory. Facts are stored bi-temporally in SQLite with episodes as provenance, and disagreements between agents become Decision units — the system never judges; the owner has the final word. It ships as the mirsad-mcp package on PyPI and runs live on Cloudflare Workers + D1, with Claude and ChatGPT connected.
projects.name: Mirsad

case.problem: AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT each start with amnesia: nothing one of them learns survives into the next session, and when two agents record different versions of a fact there is no trace of who decided what, or why.
case.solution: A shared memory hub with bi-temporal facts (every value keeps its validity window), first-class Decision units that store reasons, evidence and rejected alternatives, and a conflict queue where a challenged fact stays pending until the owner rules. Ships as an MCP server (13 tools) with a live graph viewer and a PyPI package; also deployed on Cloudflare Workers + D1.
case.role: Designed and built solo — core engine, MCP server, viewer, deployment and the release process.

projects.desc: Relative flood-risk screening with a transparent weighted model — built for screening, not prediction.
projects.long: rain2risk turns rainfall and terrain signals into a relative flood-risk picture using a published weighted model (40/20/15/15/10). The methodology is stated openly in the README, including what the tool does not claim: it screens relative risk, it does not predict floods.
projects.name: rain2risk

case.problem: Flood risk in Tunis is published as static maps and reports; a resident cannot ask 'what about my street?' and get an answer they can check.
case.solution: Relative flood-risk screening: pick a point on the map and the app scores the surrounding grid from rainfall, elevation and drainage factors, with the weighting published in the open (40/20/15/15/10) and the result labelled as relative screening, not a prediction.
case.role: Solo build — scoring backend, methodology write-up and the Leaflet map frontend.

projects.desc: Plant-disease guidance backed by a source-verified knowledge base: 18 crops, 184 verified disease records.
projects.long: CropGuide identifies possible plant diseases from a photo. Its knowledge base was rebuilt from real, source-backed records only — templated or generated records were rejected. Every one of the 184 records across 18 crops is traceable to its source.
projects.name: CropGuide

case.problem: Plant apps look at one photo and announce a disease with confidence — a guess dressed as a diagnosis, which can push a farmer toward the wrong treatment.
case.solution: Photo triage that first identifies the crop, then matches visible signs against a source-verified disease database (18 crops, 184 records), shows its evidence, and abstains — 'the photo does not give enough evidence' — when the signs are not conclusive.
case.role: Solo build — curated the verified knowledge base record by record and built the app around the abstention rule.

projects.desc: Clinic management platform with a role-aware AI assistant, an integration API, and automated appointment emails.
projects.long: A Flask clinic platform with role-based access for patients, doctors and reception. A Qwen-powered chat assistant uses role-aware tools, an integration blueprint exposes booking events, and an n8n workflow turns them into confirmation and cancellation emails — verified end-to-end with real deliveries.
projects.name: Clinique

case.problem: A small clinic runs patients, appointments and records across paper files and chat threads; nothing is searchable and reminders depend on memory.
case.solution: A clinic management platform: patients, appointments, medical records and billing with role-based access (admin, doctor, receptionist, patient), a FHIR-shaped REST API, an AI assistant whose tools are scoped to the caller's role, and n8n webhooks that fire booking confirmations and cancellations.
case.role: Solo build — Flask/SQLite platform, role-scoped chatbot tools and the n8n event integration, tested end-to-end live.

projects.desc: Full-stack health informatics and symptom-analysis application. Exploratory project.
projects.long: An exploratory full-stack health assistant: symptom analysis and health-data handling, built to learn how clinical information should (and should not) flow through an AI interface. Labelled exploratory — a proof of concept, not a medical tool.
projects.name: AI Health Assistant

case.problem: Symptom checkers rush to name a disease; for an Arabic speaker the options are worse — translated lists with no sense of urgency or safety.
case.solution: An Arabic-first health explainer (Nabd) that organizes what the user feels, explains what it may mean and what step comes next, puts safety signals first, and never claims a diagnosis.
case.role: Solo build — exploratory project; content structure and the safety-first interaction.

projects.desc: Geospatial exploration of how services and risk are distributed across places. Exploratory project.
projects.long: An exploratory GeoAI project mapping how access and risk are distributed geographically — part of an ongoing exploration of spatial data for public-good questions.
projects.name: Mapping Equity GeoAI

case.problem: Unequal access to public services is easy to assert and hard to show; without spatial evidence it stays an opinion.
case.solution: A geospatial analysis of service coverage shipped as a full documentation package — evidence register, methodology, data lineage and a validation report — so every claim in it can be re-checked.
case.role: Solo research and build — exploratory / proof of concept.

projects.desc: A modular Flask application with a layered database and service architecture. Proof of concept.
projects.long: A proof-of-concept Flask application exploring modular architecture: separated database and service layers, built as a learning exercise in structuring a Python web app.
projects.name: Pann

case.problem: A small bakery tracks stock, purchasing and profit in notebooks; reordering is guesswork and losses surface weeks late.
case.solution: BakeryERP: inventory and purchasing with predictive reorder suggestions, profitability analytics, PDF/Excel exports and role-based access (admin, manager, cashier, customer); demo accounts are only ever seeded with explicit passwords, never defaults.
case.role: Solo build — Flask ERP with database migrations and a test suite.
